CMDGLAS
USER MANUAL

COMMS shares your tablet login. The moment you sign in you are in the General Gamer Pool, so #general and #party work straight away. You do not need an org for any of that.

  1. Open the tablet and press ENTER TABLET.
  2. Sign in from the account pill at the top right.
  3. Open COMMS from the COMMS pill, or press OPEN on it.

Applications go to that org's own command, not to a site admin. Founding an org is the other route, and the founder becomes its Wing Commander once the org itself is approved.

  1. Press the ORG tab in the COMMS header.
  2. Under JOIN AN ORG pick the org, then type your real RSI handle and the callsign you want shown.
  3. Press SEND REQUEST.
  4. To start your own instead, fill in FOUND AN ORG underneath. Expect 12 to 24 hours for approval.
  1. The ORG tab — where you join or found an org.
  2. Pick the org you want to fly with.
  3. Your real RSI handle — command uses it to verify you.
  4. The callsign your wing will see.
  5. Sends your request to that org’s command.
  6. Or found your OWN org here — you become its Wing Commander.
NOTE. While you wait, #general and #party stay open to you. You lose nothing by waiting.

A party is a temporary crew. Anyone signed in can run one and no org is involved.

  1. Open CHAT and pick the #party channel.
  2. Press CREATE PARTY. A 6 character code appears. That is your party.
  3. Read the code out. Friends type it into the CODE box and press JOIN.
  4. If the leader seat is empty, anyone may press CLAIM PARTY LEAD. First claim takes it.
  1. LEAVE drops you out of the party.
  2. Your party code. Read it out; friends type it to join.
  3. The #party channel — open to every signed-in pilot, no org needed.
  4. HAND OFF gives party lead to that pilot.
  5. KICK removes them from the party.
  6. Type a base callsign here — e.g. STORM.
  7. One press numbers the whole party STORM 1, STORM 2, STORM 3…
NOTE. Drop offline and your name flashes dark orange for 30 minutes. After that the leader console releases your seat.

Type one base name and the whole party numbers off in list order. Org command and flight leads get the same menu for a squadron.

  1. Type a base callsign such as STORM into the callsign menu.
  2. Press ASSIGN. Everyone becomes STORM 1, STORM 2, STORM 3 and so on.
  3. Set any individual pilot by hand afterwards if you want to.

PARTY CMD appears in the header once you are in a party. It never mentions org chat. It is for your crew only.

  1. Press PARTY CMD.
  2. Set DAY or NIGHT for the planet you are working so everyone plans light the same way.
  3. Type into NETCALL and press TRANSMIT to reach every pilot on the party at once.
  4. Use HAND OFF to pass lead, or KICK to remove somebody.
  1. PARTY CMD appears once you are in a party.
  2. Your local time — never UTC.
  3. Day or night on the planet you are working — you set it.
  4. NETCALL: one message to every pilot in the party at once.
  5. Everybody on the party, with live status.
  6. The callsign menu again — leader only.

GROUPS lists every pilot online who wants to fly with somebody, and exactly what for.

  1. Press the GROUPS tab.
  2. Pick what you are up for, note the seats you need, press POST IT.
  3. To join somebody, choose the seat you would fill from the dropdown beside their name.
  4. Press REQUEST JOIN, or press INVITE TO PARTY to send them your code.
  1. GROUPS — who is online and what they want to fly.
  2. Say what you need — “2 turret gunners”.
  3. Pick what YOU are up for.
  4. POST IT puts you on the board for 12 hours.
  5. Pick the seat you would fill for them.
  6. REQUEST JOIN asks to join their crew.
  7. INVITE TO PARTY sends them your party code.
NOTE. Adverts expire on their own after 12 hours, so the board never shows stale posts.

A MY STATUS bar sits above the chat stream whenever you are on a party or in an org.

  1. Press MARK KIA when you die. Your name flashes KIA on every commander board until cleared.
  2. Press NEED RESCUE to raise a MEDIVAC flag beside your name.
  3. Press the same button again once you are back.
NOTE. Your commander can clear these for you, which helps when you have respawned and forgotten.

When command issues an order or an objective, a panel appears above your chat and flashes. It does not stop on its own. It stops when you answer.

WARNING. Ignoring the alert does not make it go away quietly. After two minutes without an answer the alert stops flashing and your commander board marks you IGNORED, with a notification telling them the order was never answered.
  1. Read the order: the objective, the task, the target and the seat you were given.
  2. If you can do it, press o7. That is received and complying.
  3. If you cannot, type the reason in the box. WHY flashes until you do.
  4. Press UNABLE. It stays grayed out until a reason is entered.
  5. Changed your mind? Press CHANGE MY ANSWER and answer again.
  1. The seat your squadron leader put you in.
  2. This flashes until you answer. It will not go away on its own.
  3. o7 — received and complying.
  4. UNABLE stays greyed out until a reason is entered.
  5. UNABLE needs a reason. WHY flashes until you type one.

Flight leads and element leads are not org command, so you get a smaller panel with exactly what the job needs. It sits at the bottom of the ORG tab.

  1. Open the ORG tab.
  2. Read the objective your squadron was given, and your own seat.
  3. Check each of your pilots: their seat, and whether they answered.
  4. Set tactical callsigns for your squadron from the callsign menu.
  1. Your own panel — flight and element leads only.
  2. The objective your squadron was given.
  3. The pilots under you, their seats and their answers.
  4. You can set tactical callsigns for your squadron.
NOTE. Seats are set by your squadron leader. If a seat is wrong, message them. The envelope button beside a name jumps into their channel.

The ORG tab becomes a command console for Wing Commanders and Squadron Leaders. This is where the wing gets built.

  1. Approve applicants after setting their rank and squadron.
  2. Move anyone between squadrons with their squadron dropdown.
  3. Press LEAD on a pilot to make them that squadron leader.
  4. Pair pilots into elements with the element dropdown.
  5. Give a squadron its order: pick the task, type the target, press SET.
  1. The rank they will hold.
  2. The squadron they land in.
  3. Approve an applicant — pick their rank and squadron first.
  4. And the target — a callsign, gamertag or place.
  5. Give this squadron its order.
  6. SET pushes it to every pilot in that squadron instantly.
  7. Change a pilot’s rank.
  8. Move a pilot to another squadron.
  9. LEAD makes that pilot the squadron leader.
  10. Pair a pilot to an element lead — this is who they fly on.

The whole operation on one screen: local clock, planetside day or night, force status, step off countdown, netcall and orders readback.

  1. Press ORG CMD in the header.
  2. Check FORCE STATUS for who is on station, assigned, KIA or needing a medivac.
  3. Set the planetside day or night condition for the op.
  4. Use NETCALL to reach every station at once.
  5. Read ORDERS READBACK to confirm what each squadron is doing.
  1. ORG CMD — the wing commander’s console.
  2. Local time.
  3. Planetside day/night for this operation.
  4. Countdown to the step-off time you set in the OP PLANNER.
  5. Force status: on station, assigned, KIA, MEDIVAC.
  6. NETCALL — all stations, one transmission.
  7. Orders readback: what every squadron is doing right now.
  8. Everyone under your command, grouped by squadron and element.

Orders tell a squadron what to do. Objectives tell them what to achieve, and they flow down the chain to the assignment sheet.

  1. Type the objective name, for example SEIZE KAREAH.
  2. Choose PRIMARY, SECONDARY or CONTINGENCY.
  3. Assign it to a squadron now, or leave it and assign later.
  4. Add the detail line: what done looks like.
  5. Press CREATE OBJECTIVE.
  6. Press ASSIGNMENT SHEET on that objective to seat the squadron pilots.
  1. Name the objective.
  2. Primary, secondary or contingency.
  3. Hand it to a squadron.
  4. CREATE OBJECTIVE writes it to the board.
  5. Optional detail — what “done” looks like.
  6. Reassign the objective to a different squadron at any time.
  7. ASSIGNMENT SHEET — open it to seat that squadron’s pilots.
  8. Tick it complete.
  9. Scrub it.

The pop up sheet for whoever owns a squadron. Squadron leaders use it for their own squadron. The Wing Commander can open any of them.

  1. Open it from the objective ASSIGNMENT SHEET button.
  2. Pick the seat each pilot will fill.
  3. Watch the answer badge beside each name: o7, UNABLE with the reason, or awaiting a reply.
  4. Press SEND SHEET TO SQUADRON to post every seat to the org channel.
  1. Which squadron you are seating, and how many are seated.
  2. CLOSE.
  3. The objective this squadron was given.
  4. Pick the seat this pilot fills.
  5. Clear their seat.
  6. Their answer to the last order: o7, UNABLE, or no reply yet.
  7. SEND SHEET posts every seat to the org channel.

The planner pulls assignments, orders, callsigns and elements live from the board at the moment you press a button.

WARNING. DISTRIBUTE is real. Every member on the channel gets it immediately, so do not press it while you are experimenting.
  1. Name the operation and set the step off time in your own local time.
  2. Pick the channel the op runs on and write your intent.
  3. EXPORT PDF opens a printable op order. Use your browser Save as PDF.
  4. EXPORT EXCEL downloads the assignment sheet as a spreadsheet.
  5. DISTRIBUTE TO ORG posts the whole op order to every member at once.
  1. Step-off time in YOUR local time.
  2. Name the operation.
  3. Which channel the op runs on.
  4. Commander’s intent.
  5. DISTRIBUTE sends the whole op order to every member at once.
  6. EXPORT PDF — a printable op order.
  7. EXPORT EXCEL — the assignment sheet as a spreadsheet.

Both consoles carry it now.

  1. On PARTY CMD, press KICK beside a name to remove them from the party.
  2. On ORG CMD, press KICK to remove a pilot from the org. They lose org channels immediately and must re-apply.
  3. Wing Commanders cannot be kicked from the console.

Home is six pills. The three across the middle are the ones you use constantly.

  1. INGAME TOOLS holds every reference page, plus the full width SHIP LOADOUTS bar.
  2. The center pill carries GATHER, BUY, NOTES, ORG/PARTY and STREAM.
  3. The COMMS pill is your org and party chat.

A page in the center pill that answers three things at a glance: who you are in the wing, how the force is doing, and what you personally were told to do.

  1. Press ORG/PARTY in the center pill.
  2. Switch between PARTY VIEW and ORG VIEW with the two buttons.
  3. Press FULL ROSTER for everyone and their status.
  4. Press MSG ORG or MSG PARTY to jump into comms.

Every hull shows burst DPS, alpha strike, sustained DPS, hull HP and shield pool, read live and stamped with the game version.

  1. Open Ship Loadouts from the INGAME TOOLS bar.
  2. Add your hulls once with ADD SHIPS.
  3. Tap any hull to open it. Totals sit at the top.
NOTE. If the data source cannot be reached the panel says so. It never shows a guessed number.

Shield, power plant, cooler, quantum drive and radar are dropdowns. Every option reads name, then size, then class and grade, for example FR-66 then S1 then MIL-A.

  1. Open a hull and look at the SYSTEMS block.
  2. Parts that fit your slot are grouped at the top of each list.
  3. The trolley button pushes that part to your BUY list.

Pick your ship and any target. Both are given the best gun in the game for every hardpoint they carry, turrets included, then you get a straight answer.

WARNING. It ignores shield regeneration, damage falloff, resistances, ammo and pilot skill. Pilot skill decides most real fights. Treat it as a sanity check, not a promise.
  1. Scroll to THREAT CHECK under the ship totals.
  2. Pick your ship on the left and a target on the right.
  3. Press CHECK IT.
  4. Read the seconds each side needs to kill the other, then the verdict.

For the hull you have open: quantum tank and range, and the hydrogen tank it carries today against the one 4.10 is testing.

WARNING. These are EPTU test numbers for 4.10 set against live 4.9. They can change before 4.10 ships. The panel says so every time it renders.
  1. Open any hull in Ship Loadouts.
  2. The FUEL AND ENDURANCE panel sits under the ship totals.

The whole chain of command on one screen, with your own position highlighted.

  1. Press WING in the COMMS header.
  2. Wing Command sits at the top, then each squadron and its leader, then elements and pilots.

Most tool pages carry an amber PUSH TO HUD → button at the top. It takes the rows you picked on that page and drops them straight into the HUD pill’s GATHER & BUY list, then puts you back on the HUD. Nothing is summarised and nothing is invented — what you see on the page is what lands on the list.

  1. Open any tool page from the INGAME TOOLS bar — Mining, Harvestables, Blueprints, Salvage, Hauling, Ship Loadouts and the rest.
  2. Tap a row in any table on that page. It turns into a tag on the PICKED bar so you can see exactly what you have selected.
  3. Tap more rows to add them. Tap a tag again, or CLEAR, to drop it.
  4. Tap PUSH TO HUD →, top-left of the page.
  5. You land back on the HUD with the pill switched to GATHER & BUY. Your items are on the list.

Pushing the same item twice does nothing — the list refuses duplicates and tells you so.

NOTE. If you tap PUSH TO HUD without picking anything first, it says Nothing picked — click a row first and does not touch your list.

The pages that carry the button:

  1. Mining
  2. Harvestables
  3. Blueprints
  4. Craft Calculator
  5. Salvage
  6. Hauling
  7. Ship Loadouts
  8. Ship DB
  9. Inventory
  10. Contracts
  11. Starmap
  12. Reputation
  13. Gather & Buy

The Craft Calculator works differently, on purpose. Its catalog holds over a thousand blueprint rows, so it does not push those. It pushes the materials the calculator worked out for the blueprints you selected, and it pins those blueprint names as PUSHED tags at the top of the pill so you can see what the list is for.

  1. Open the Craft Calculator from the INGAME TOOLS bar.
  2. Set a quantity on every blueprint you intend to build, using + and −.
  3. Tap PUSH TO HUD →, top-left of the page.
  4. The toast tells you exactly what went across — how many materials, and how many blueprint names were pinned.
NOTE. Blueprints you select in the Craft Calculator already feed their materials into the gather list on their own. The button is there so you can send them deliberately, pin the blueprint names, and get back to the HUD in one tap.
CAUTION. CLEAR on the gather list wipes the whole list at once. There is no undo. If you only want one item gone, remove that item rather than clearing.

Every line on the HUD’s GATHER & BUY list carries a row of small blue buttons underneath it. Each button opens the exact table that holds that item, scrolls straight to its row and outlines it. A button is only shown when there is a real row to land on.

  1. Open the HUD pill and tap the GATHER & BUY tab, first in the row.
  2. Find the material you want on the list.
  3. Tap a button underneath it. The page opens, the section it lives in opens itself, and the row is outlined in blue.
  4. Tap RETURN TO HUD, right-hand end of the strip at the top of the page, to come back to the same pill tab you left from.

What each button means:

  1. LASER — Mining, ROCKS REF. The laser power it takes to crack it.
  2. LOCATIONS — Harvestables, SHIP-MINEABLE ORES. Where the rock spawns.
  3. HAND GEM — Harvestables, FPS HAND-MINABLE GEMS. Pick it up on foot.
  4. ROC GEM — Harvestables, ROC GEMS. ROC-mine it.
  5. HARVEST — Harvestables, HARVESTABLES + COLLECTIBLES. Hand-collect it.
  6. BUY — Hauling, USER-REPORTED ROUTES. Buy it instead, with a price and an SCU count.
  7. BLUEPRINT — Blueprints catalog. What it builds into.
  8. SHIP BUILDER and SHIP DB — for ships and components on the buy side.

A material can carry several buttons because it can be had several ways. Iron reads LASER · LOCATIONS · BUY — crack it, find it, or just buy it. Aphorite reads HAND GEM only, because that is the one way you get it.

NOTE. A line reading no source page carries this item means exactly that — nothing in the tablet holds a row for it. It is not an error, and the item stays on your list.
NOTE. The Hauling page shows one set of user-reported routes at a time. If an item sits in a set the page currently has switched off, the button opens the page and tells you so rather than leaving you on a page that did not move.
Nothing matches that. Clear the search or pick a different role.
